m: Gümüşhane Province (Turkish: Gümüşhane ili) is a province in northern Turkey, bordering Bayburt to the east, Trabzon to the north, Giresun and Erzincan to the west. Its area is 6,668 km2, and its population is 144,544 (2022). The population was 186,953 in 2000. Gümüşhane is the capital city of the province. The name Gümüşhane means silver house. The city has a rich mining (silver and bronze) history and was the source of exports for Trabzon. The current Governor is Alper Tanrısever, appointed in August 2023.

e-artabel-golleri-tabiat-parki: A nature park in Gümüşhane made up of glacial lakes of different sizes among high mountains. People come for hiking and camping in summer.
e-santa-harabeleri: Ruins of stone houses, churches and a school from an old Greek settlement in the forests around Dumanlı village, Gümüşhane. The highland and nature around it also draw visitors.
Q4810702:
Karaca Cave (Turkish: Karaca Mağarası) is a network of caves located near the town of Torul in Gümüşhane Province, Turkey.
Although the cave was known to the people living in that region, it became open to tourism as a result of the scientific research conducted by Sukru Eroz, a geological engineer from Cebeli Village, between the years 1983-1990. Prof. Dr. Remzi Dilek and his team from the Department of Geological Engineering at the (Karadeniz Technical University) contributed a lot of research and scientific studies of the cave. As a result of these studies, it was opened to tourism in 1996 after the Ministry of Culture and Tourism was informed and the cave was officially registered.
Q31190853: Tomara Waterfall is in the Şiran district of Gümüşhane, in the valley of the Tomara stream, a tributary of the Kelkit. It is named after the tomara plant that grows nearby.
Q2211116: Located in Turkey, the settlement of Satala, according to the ancient geographers, was situated in a valley surrounded by mountains, a little north of the Euphrates, where the road from Trapezus to Samosata crossed the boundary of the Roman Empire, when it was a bishopric, which remains a Latin Catholic titular see. Later it was connected with Nicopolis by two highways. Satala is now Sadak, a village of 348 inhabitants (2022), in the Kelkit District of Gümüşhane Province in Turkey.
Q629897: Patara was a small ancient city in ancient Cappadocia or Lesser Armenia, (Tab. Peut.), later in Pontus. The city lay on the major trade road from Trapezus on the Black Sea to Satala, and thence to Lake Van.
Q96023275: Limni Lake is in the village of Zigana in the Torul district of Gümüşhane, surrounded by spruce, Scots pine, juniper, fir, blackberry and purple- and yellow-flowered rhododendron. Sources give its altitude as anything from 1,700 to 2,100 metres.
Q97387392: Imera Monastery, or the Monastery of St John Prodromos, is in the village of Olucak, Gümüşhane. According to written sources it was built in 1350 and renovated in 1859 by the nun Roxane.
Q97207430: Canca Castle, or Tzaniha Castle, is built on rocky ground west of Gümüşhane, at an altitude of 1,530 metres. A restoration contract worth 1.8 million lira was tendered in 2018. The partly rounded castle is built of rubble stone.
Q97205392: Kov Castle is a castle 22 km south-east of central Gümüşhane.
Q97206355: Torul Castle, also called Toğrul or Ardasa Castle, is east of Torul, Gümüşhane. Now in ruins, it was built as a fire tower for signalling. Its gate is on the east side, and it stands about 200 metres high; its walls are of rubble and dressed stone in the colour of the natural rock.
Q97387317: Tohumoğlu Bridge crosses the Harşit stream 17 km east of Gümüşhane. It is about 65 metres long and 5.35 metres wide. Together with the Gümüşhane Bridge, it was built in October 1575 by Ferruh Zad Oğlu Halebi. It has two round arches and a flood opening in its pier; the rubble-paved deck slopes.
